correctness.rationale: The two finite exhaustive enumeration methods produce the same 168 canonical hyperovals; the first checks all 54,264 six-subsets, the other proves unique completion of all 2,520 four-arcs. Both calculate all 14,028 pair relations and 4/5/16/11 common-neighbour counts. This proves every nonedge has a common neighbour and diameter two, while uniqueness of four-arc completion excludes smaller swaps. Exact integer matrix polynomial and traces fix spectral multiplicities; checkers and outputs are included.

Classical counts, orbit partition and intersection frequencies are credited and not counted as new. value.rationale: Hyperovals are canonical maximal finite arcs, and unique four-arc completion imposes a sharp intrinsic barrier to one- or two-point moves. Proving all 168 states reachable in at most two moves at the first permitted exchange length, with their exact two-walk profile and spectrum, describes an essential finite rigidity/mobility threshold rather than a random parameter slice. It remains useful without a general-order extension.
